claim: Trichomonas vaginalis is the etiologic agent of the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infection worldwide.
source: Trichomonas vaginalis, the etiologic agent of the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infection worldwide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about T. vaginalis.

claim: There is an estimated annual prevalence of 276 million new cases of trichomoniasis.
source: With an estimated annual prevalence of 276 million new cases, mixed infections with different parasite strains are expected.
evidence: This statistic is cited in the abstract and introduction with reference to WHO, 2018.

claim: Different T. vaginalis strains can communicate through the formation of cytoneme-like membranous cell connections.
source: Here, we demonstrated that different T. vaginalis strains can communicate through the formation of cytoneme-like membranous cell connections.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Cytoneme formation of CDC1132 strain is affected in the presence of G3 or B7RC2 strains.
source: We showed that cytonemes formation of an adherent parasite strain (CDC1132) is affected in the presence of a different strain (G3 or B7RC2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: The effect of inter-strain communication on cytoneme formation is contact-independent.
source: Our findings provide evidence that this effect is contact-independent and that extracellular vesicles (EVs) are responsible, at least in part, of the communication among strains.
evidence: This is demonstrated through transwell experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Extracellular vesicles are responsible, at least in part, for communication among T. vaginalis strains.
source: Our findings provide evidence that this effect is contact-independent and that extracellular vesicles (EVs) are responsible, at least in part, of the communication among strains.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing that isolated EVs can induce cytoneme formation (Figure 4C).

claim: EVs isolated from G3, B7RC2, and CDC1132 strains contain highly distinct repertoires of proteins.
source: We found that EVs isolated from G3, B7RC2, and CDC1132 strains contain a highly distinct repertoire of proteins, some of them involved in signaling and communication, among other functions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Parasite adherence to host cells is affected by communication between strains.
source: Finally, we showed that parasite adherence to host cells is affected by communication between strains as binding of adherent T. vaginalis CDC1132 strain to prostate cells is significantly higher in the presence of G3 or B7RC2 strains.
evidence: This is demonstrated by attachment assays shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Binding of CDC1132 strain to prostate cells is significantly higher in the presence of G3 or B7RC2 strains.
source: binding of adherent T. vaginalis CDC1132 strain to prostate cells is significantly higher in the presence of G3 or B7RC2 strains.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B with statistical significance.

claim: A poorly adherent parasite strain (G3) adheres more strongly to prostate cells in the presence of an adherent strain.
source: We also observed that a poorly adherent parasite strain (G3) adheres more strongly to prostate cells in the presence of an adherent strain.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6D showing increased G3 attachment when co-cultured with CDC1132.

claim: Mixed infections with several T. vaginalis parasite strains are anticipated due to the parasite's great prevalence in some communities.
source: Due to its great prevalence in some communities, mixed infections with several parasite strains are anticipated.
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference based on prevalence data.

claim: An analysis of 211 T. vaginalis samples isolated in five different continents identified 23 cases of mixed infections (10.9%).
source: In this sense, an analysis performed of 211 T. vaginalis samples isolated in five different continents identified 23 cases of mixed infections (10.9%; Conrad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited data from Conrad et al., 2012.

claim: T. vaginalis infection can cause multiple symptoms and pathologies including vaginitis, urethritis, prostatitis, low birth weight infants and preterm delivery, premature rupture of membranes, and infertility.
source: Although asymptomatic infection is common, multiple symptoms and pathologies can arise in both men and women, including vaginitis, urethritis, prostatitis, low birth weight infants and preterm delivery, premature rupture of membranes, and infertility (Fichorova, 2009; Swygard et al., 2004).
evidence: This is cited information from Fichorova, 2009 and Swygard et al., 2004.

claim: T. vaginalis has emerged as an important cofactor in amplifying HIV spread.
source: T. vaginalis has also emerged as an important cofactor in amplifying the HIV spread as individuals infected with T. vaginalis have a significantly increased incidence of HIV transmission (McClelland et al., 2007; Van Der Pol et al., 2008).
evidence: This is cited from McClelland et al., 2007 and Van Der Pol et al., 2008.

claim: Individuals infected with T. vaginalis have a significantly increased incidence of HIV transmission.
source: individuals infected with T. vaginalis have a significantly increased incidence of HIV transmission (McClelland et al., 2007; Van Der Pol et al., 2008).
evidence: This is cited from McClelland et al., 2007 and Van Der Pol et al., 2008.

claim: T. vaginalis infection increases the risk of cervical and aggressive prostate cancer.
source: Additionally, T. vaginalis infection increases the risk of cervical and aggressive prostate cancer (Gander et al., 2009; Twu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Gander et al., 2009 and Twu et al., 2014.

claim: The highly adherent strains B7RC2 and CDC1132 have greater number of filopodia and cytonemes compared to poorly adherent strains G3 and NYU209.
source: When the number of membrane protrusions was quantified, we observed that the highly adherent strains B7RC2 and CDC1132 have greater number of filopodia and cytonemes compared to poorly adherent strains G3 and NYU209 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantification data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Multiple filopodia and cytonemes originated from the surface of highly adherent CDC1132 parasites.
source: In concordance, SEM revealed that multiple filopodia and cytonemes originated from the surface of highly adherent CDC1132 parasites and almost no such protrusions were observed in the poorly adherent G3 strain (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown by SEM images in Figure 1B.

claim: Almost no filopodia and cytonemes protrusions were observed in the poorly adherent G3 strain.
source: SEM revealed that multiple filopodia and cytonemes originated from the surface of highly adherent CDC1132 parasites and almost no such protrusions were observed in the poorly adherent G3 strain (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown by SEM images in Figure 1B.

claim: Cytonemes in T. vaginalis can extend up to 4.6 µm in length.
source: These tubular extensions appear to be close ended and can be seen protruding from the region where the flagella emerge as well as from the cell body, with a length up to 4.6 µm (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This measurement is reported from SEM observations.

claim: Cytonemes from the flagellar base in T. vaginalis are unbranched with homogeneous morphology and size ranging from 70 nm to 100 nm in thickness.
source: The cytonemes from the flagellar base appear unbranched, displaying a homogeneous morphology and size ranging from 70 nm to 100 nm in thickness (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is measured from SEM images.

claim: The ultrastructural features of T. vaginalis cytonemes are similar to flagellar projections previously described in Tritrichomonas foetus.
source: Their ultrastructural features are similar to those flagellar projections previously described in the related veterinary trichomonad Tritrichomonas foetus (Benchimol et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparison to previously published work by Benchimol et al., 2021.

claim: Tubular extensions from the cell body in T. vaginalis are heterogeneous, with diameters that vary from 70 nm to 540 nm.
source: However, the tubular extensions from the cell body are heterogeneous, with diameters that vary from 70 nm to 540 nm and some of them furcated (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is measured from SEM images.

claim: The number of parasites containing cytonemes is higher at 10^6 parasites/ml.
source: As can be observed in Figure 2, the number of parasites containing cytonemes is higher at 106 parasites/ml (Figure 2C); a cell culture condition where usually clumps are formed (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C with quantification data.

claim: Cytonemes are frequently observed connecting two parasites.
source: Consistent with this, cytonemes are frequently observed connecting two parasites (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in SEM images in Figure 2D.

claim: The closed tip of cytonemes was frequently seen in contact with any region of the surface of an adjacent parasite.
source: The closed tip of cytonemes was frequently seen in contact with any region of the surface of an adjacent parasite (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), including other cytonemes (Figure 2A and D).
evidence: This is observed in SEM images.

claim: CDC1132 parasites are able to interact and form clumps with parasites from B7RC2 or G3 strains.
source: As observed in Figure 3A, CDC1132 parasites are able to interact and form clumps with parasites from B7RC2 or G3 strains (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in co-culture experiments in Figure 3A.

claim: The number of CDC1132 parasites in the bottom of the well containing cytonemes and filopodia significantly increases when G3 or B7RC2 strains are loaded in the inserts.
source: As can be observed in Figure 4A, the number of receiving parasites containing cytonemes and filopodia significantly increases when G3 or B7RC2 strains are loaded in the inserts, compared to the control where CDC1132 strain was loaded in the chamber.
evidence: This is shown in transwell experiments in Figure 4A with statistical significance.

claim: The number of CDC1132 parasites containing cytonemes and filopodia is significantly higher when VPS32 overexpressing parasites (G3 strain) are loaded into the inserts compared to control parasites.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, the number of CDC1132 parasites in the bottom of the well containing cytonemes and filopodia is significantly higher when VPS32 overexpressing parasites (G3 strain) are loaded into the inserts compared to the incubation with G3 parasites transfected with empty vector (EpNEO - control parasites) or G3 wild-type parasites (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B with statistical analysis.

claim: VPS32-overexpressing parasites produce more EVs than EpNEO parasites.
source: As VPS32-overexpressing produce more EVs than EpNEO parasites, these results may indicate that released EVs have a role in the formation of membrane protrusions in recipient parasites.
evidence: This is stated based on previous work (Salas et al., 2021) showing VPS32's role in EV biogenesis.

claim: The addition of 10 µg of EVs from G3 or B7RC2, but not EVs from CDC1132, increased the formation of cytonemes and filopodia of CDC1132 recipient parasites.
source: The addition of 10 µg of EVs from G3 or B7RC2, but not EVs from CDC1132, increased the formation of cytonemes and filopodia of CDC1132 recipient parasites (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C with quantification data.

claim: 1317 proteins were identified in EVs enriched samples isolated from G3 strain.
source: Overall, we identified 1317, 954, and 375 proteins in the EVs enriched samples isolated from G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2 strains, respectively (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is from mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 954 proteins were identified in EVs enriched samples isolated from CDC1132 strain.
source: Overall, we identified 1317, 954, and 375 proteins in the EVs enriched samples isolated from G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2 strains, respectively (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is from mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 375 proteins were identified in EVs enriched samples isolated from B7RC2 strain.
source: Overall, we identified 1317, 954, and 375 proteins in the EVs enriched samples isolated from G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2 strains, respectively (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is from mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Only a core of 346 proteins is shared among EVs isolated from different strains.
source: When the protein content was analyzed, the results indicated that only a core of 346 proteins is shared among EVs isolated from different strains (Figure 5B) as only.
evidence: This is shown in the Venn diagram in Figure 5B.

claim: EVs derived from G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2 strains contain several proteins that play crucial roles in regulating the formation of filopodia and/or cytonemes in other cells.
source: Remarkably, EVs derived from parasites from G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2 strains contain several proteins that play crucial roles in regulating the formation of filopodia and/or cytonemes in other cells.
evidence: This is based on identification of specific protein families in the proteomics data.

claim: EVs from G3 contain 12 Rho proteins, EVs from CDC1132 contain 11 Rho proteins, and EVs from B7RC2 contain 5 Rho proteins.
source: These proteins encompass Rho proteins (12, 11, and 5 members in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), Ras family proteins (13, 9, and 3 members in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), Calreticulin (1, 2, and 1 member in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), and profilin (5, 5, and 4 members in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), as detailed in Supplementary file 1.
evidence: This is from the proteomics analysis detailed in Supplementary file 1.

claim: EVs from G3 contain 13 Ras family proteins, EVs from CDC1132 contain 9 Ras family proteins, and EVs from B7RC2 contain 3 Ras family proteins.
source: These proteins encompass Rho proteins (12, 11, and 5 members in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), Ras family proteins (13, 9, and 3 members in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), Calreticulin (1, 2, and 1 member in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), and profilin (5, 5, and 4 members in G3, CDC1132, and B7RC2, respectively), as detailed in Supplementary file 1.
evidence: This is from the proteomics analysis detailed in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The percentage of amoeboid CDC1132 cells is higher when G3 or B7RC2 are loaded on the inserts compared to the presence of CDC1132 in the chamber.
source: Using a cell culture insert assay, we observed that the percentage of amoeboid CDC1132 cells is higher when G3 or B7RC2 are loaded on the inserts compared to the presence of CDC1132 in the chamber (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A with quantification data.

claim: Communication among different T. vaginalis strains induces amoeboid transformation in recipient parasites.
source: These results indicate that communication among different T. vaginalis strain induce ameboid transformation in recipient parasites.
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Cytonemes protruding from both flagellar base and cell body of CDC1132 were frequently observed in contact with BPH1 cells by SEM.
source: In concordance with our previous results demonstrating that parasite communication induces cytoneme formation (Figure 3) and increase in host-cell adherence (Figure 6B), we frequently observed cytonemes protruding from both flagellar base and cell body of CDC1132 in contact with BPH1 cells by SEM (Figure 6C and Video 2).
evidence: This is shown in SEM images in Figure 6C.

claim: Co-incubation of CDC1132 strain with G3 parasites resulted in a twofold increase in G3 attachment to BPH1.
source: Importantly, co-incubation of CDC1132 strain with G3 parasites resulted in a twofold increase in G3 attachment to BPH1 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D with quantification data.

claim: Conditioned media from a highly adherent strain can increase parasite attachment to host cells of a less adherent strain.
source: In concordance with previous reports (Twu et al., 2013), these data indicate that conditions media from a highly adherent strain can increase parasite attachment to host cells of a less adherent strain.
evidence: This is stated as consistent with previous work by Twu et al., 2013.

claim: Mycoplasma was not detected in the supernatant of G3, B7RC2, or CDC1132 strains.
source: As can be observed in Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Mycoplasma was not detected in the supernatant of any of the analyzed strains.
evidence: This is shown by PCR results in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: EVs released by isolates with distinct phenotypic characteristics can affect the behavior of recipient parasite.
source: The findings indicate that EVs released by isolates with distinct phenotypic characteristics can affect the behavior of recipient parasite, which could have significant clinical implications in the context of mixed infections.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Filopodia are thin cellular extensions that have been observed in many cell types.
source: Among different types of cellular protrusions, filopodia are thin cellular extensions that have been observed in many cell types and have been assigned different roles like cell migration, cell adhesion, force generation, wound healing, environmental sensing, antigen presentation, and neuronal pathfinding (Roy and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Roy and Kornberg, 2015.

claim: Filopodia have been assigned different roles including cell migration, cell adhesion, force generation, wound healing, environmental sensing, antigen presentation, and neuronal pathfinding.
source: filopodia are thin cellular extensions that have been observed in many cell types and have been assigned different roles like cell migration, cell adhesion, force generation, wound healing, environmental sensing, antigen presentation, and neuronal pathfinding (Roy and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Roy and Kornberg, 2015.

claim: Filopodia are actin-based structures.
source: Although their physical properties vary (2–400 µm in length and 0.1–0.3 µm diameter), all are actin-based, they extend and retract at velocities that have been measured as much as 25 µm/min, and their tips can contact other cells (Roy and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Roy and Kornberg, 2015.

claim: Cytonemes are considered as thin specialized filopodia that traffic signaling proteins such as morphogens, growth factors, and cell determination factors.
source: Specifically, cytonemes are considered as thin specialized filopodia that have been shown to traffic signaling proteins such as morphogens, growth factors, and cell determination factors (Roy and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Roy and Kornberg, 2015.

claim: Cytonemes have similar diameters to conventional filopodia (typically smaller than 200 nm).
source: Although cytonemes have similar diameters to conventional filopodia (typically smaller than 200 nm), they have the potential to extend up to ~300 nm from the originating cell body and have been observed in both vertebrate and invertebrate systems (Kornberg and Roy, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Kornberg and Roy, 2014.

claim: Cytonemes have the potential to extend up to ~300 nm from the originating cell body.
source: Although cytonemes have similar diameters to conventional filopodia (typically smaller than 200 nm), they have the potential to extend up to ~300 nm from the originating cell body and have been observed in both vertebrate and invertebrate systems (Kornberg and Roy, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from Kornberg and Roy, 2014.

claim: EVs are a group of heterogeneous particles formed by a lipid bilayer containing proteins and nucleic acids.
source: They are a group of heterogeneous particles formed by a lipid bilayer containing proteins and nucleic acids (Abels and Breakefield, 2016; Yáñez-Mó et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Abels and Breakefield, 2016 and Yáñez-Mó et al., 2015.

claim: Exosomes are formed due to plasma membrane invagination into multivesicular bodies with size ranging from 40 to 100 nm.
source: Among the various subtypes of EVs, the particles can be defined according to the mode of biogenesis, size, and function into three major categories: (1) exosomes formed due to plasma membrane invagination into multivesicular bodies with size ranging from 40 to 100 nm; (2) microvesicles (MVs), also called shedding vesicles, microparticles or ectosomes, originated from the budding and extrusion of the plasma membrane, with sizes between 50 and 1000 nm and an asymmetric structure; and (3) apoptotic bodies, with greater sizes (up to 1000 nm) originated from cells in the process of programmed cell death (Kalra et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from Kalra et al., 2012.

claim: Microvesicles originated from the budding and extrusion of the plasma membrane, with sizes between 50 and 1000 nm.
source: microvesicles (MVs), also called shedding vesicles, microparticles or ectosomes, originated from the budding and extrusion of the plasma membrane, with sizes between 50 and 1000 nm and an asymmetric structure
evidence: This is cited from Kalra et al., 2012.

claim: The formation of EVs in T. vaginalis increases in the presence of host cells.
source: Specifically, in T. vaginalis, the analysis of EVs, both exosomes and MVs, has become a very exciting field in the study of parasite: host interaction, as it has been shown that the formation of EVs increase in the presence of host cells and modulate parasite adherence (Nievas et al., 2020; Nievas et al., 2018a; Olmos-Ortiz et al., 2017; Rai and Johnson, 2019; Twu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: EVs in T. vaginalis modulate parasite adherence.
source: it has been shown that the formation of EVs increase in the presence of host cells and modulate parasite adherence (Nievas et al., 2020; Nievas et al., 2018a; Olmos-Ortiz et al., 2017; Rai and Johnson, 2019; Twu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: Formation of clumps in T. vaginalis cell culture generally correlates with the ability of the strain to adhere and be cytotoxic to host cells.
source: As previously shown (Coceres et al., 2015; Lustig et al., 2013), formation of clumps in cell culture generally correlates with the ability of the strain to adhere and be cytotoxic to host cells.
evidence: This is cited from Coceres et al., 2015 and Lustig et al., 2013.

claim: Highly adherent T. vaginalis strains tend to aggregate when cultured in the absence of host cells.
source: Specifically, highly adherent strains tend to aggregate when cultured in the absence of host cells in contrast to poorly adherent strains that generally do not form clumps in vitro (Coceres et al., 2015; Nievas et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is cited from Coceres et al., 2015 and Nievas et al., 2018b.

claim: Poorly adherent T. vaginalis strains generally do not form clumps in vitro.
source: in contrast to poorly adherent strains that generally do not form clumps in vitro (Coceres et al., 2015; Nievas et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is cited from Coceres et al., 2015 and Nievas et al., 2018b.

claim: Cytonemes might be involved in parasite-parasite communication in T. vaginalis.
source: These results suggest that cytonemes might be involved in parasite: parasite communication.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cytoneme formation correlates with clump formation.

claim: Cytonemes are specifically involved in parasite-parasite communication in T. vaginalis.
source: These results suggest that cytonemes are specifically involved in parasite: parasite communication.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effect on cytonemes versus filopodia during inter-strain communication.

claim: The maximum effect of EVs in T. vaginalis was observed at 9 μg.
source: Similar as previously described where the maximum effect of EVs in T. vaginalis was observed at 9 μg (Twu et al., 2013), we did not observe any additional increase in the formation of cytonemes and filopodia when increased the concentration of EVs to 20 μg (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is cited from Twu et al., 2013 and confirmed by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Specific molecules are loaded in EVs isolated from different T. vaginalis strains.
source: These results confirm that EVs are key factors for communication between different strains and suggest that specific molecules are loaded in EVs isolated from different strains.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of EVs from different strains.

claim: The biological processes detected in the different EVs preparations are highly conserved despite differences in protein identity.
source: Even while the identity of proteins detected in the EVs of each strain differs from one another, the GO analysis indicates that the biological processes detected in the different EVs preparations are highly conserved (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is shown by GO analysis in Figure 5D.

claim: EVs may be selectively loaded with specific groups of proteins that exert specific functions.
source: These data suggest that EVs may be selectively loaded with specific groups of proteins that may be thus exerting specific functions, serving as part of a strain-specific sorting pathway for delivery of biologically active molecules to neighboring cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the proteomics data showing distinct protein cargo.

claim: For extracellular pathogens such as T. vaginalis, the ability of a parasite to adhere to the host is likely a determinant of pathogenesis.
source: For extracellular pathogens such as T. vaginalis, the ability of a parasite to adhere to the host is likely a determinant of pathogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about pathogenesis.

claim: T. vaginalis changes morphology within minutes from flagellated free-swimming cell to amoeboid-adherent stage to attach to host cells.
source: To attach, T. vaginalis changes morphology within minutes: the flagellated free-swimming cell converts into the amoeboid-adherent stage (Kusdian et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Kusdian et al., 2013.

claim: There are connections between pathogenesis and amoeboid morphological transitions in T. vaginalis.
source: As it is well established the connections between pathogenesis and ameboid morphological transitions in T. vaginalis (Kusdian et al., 2013) and our results here, we investigated whether the presence of a different parasite strain could affect the ability of the recipient parasite to convert to an ameboid form (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is cited from Kusdian et al., 2013.

claim: T. vaginalis amoeboid forms have been previously associated with parasite adherence.
source: As T. vaginalis amoeboid forms have been previously associated to parasite adherence (Arroyo et al., 1993), we then evaluated if communication among strains could affect the adherence of CDC1132 to BPH1 prostate cells.
evidence: This is cited from Arroyo et al., 1993.

claim: T. vaginalis establishes an endosymbiotic relationship with some Mycoplasma species.
source: It has been reported that T. vaginalis establishes an endosymbiotic relationship with some Mycoplasma species (Dessì et al., 2019; Fichorova et al., 2017; Margarita et al., 2020) and that the presence of the bacteria can alter the parasite's ability to adhere to human epithelial cells (Margarita et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: The presence of Mycoplasma can alter T. vaginalis ability to adhere to human epithelial cells.
source: the presence of the bacteria can alter the parasite's ability to adhere to human epithelial cells (Margarita et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from Margarita et al., 2022.

claim: Communication between Trypanosoma brucei parasites modulates quorum sensing-mediated differentiation into the tsetse fly transmissible short-stumpy developmental form in the mammalian bloodstream.
source: As example, communication between Trypanosoma brucei parasites modulates the quorum sensing-mediated differentiation of into the tsetse fly transmissible short-stumpy developmental form in the mammalian bloodstream (Mony et al., 2014) as well as social motility exhibited by procyclic forms in the insect vector midgut (Oberholzer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is cited from Mony et al., 2014.

claim: Communication between Trypanosoma brucei parasites modulates social motility exhibited by procyclic forms in the insect vector midgut.
source: communication between Trypanosoma brucei parasites modulates the quorum sensing-mediated differentiation of into the tsetse fly transmissible short-stumpy developmental form in the mammalian bloodstream (Mony et al., 2014) as well as social motility exhibited by procyclic forms in the insect vector midgut (Oberholzer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is cited from Oberholzer et al., 2010.

claim: Plasmodium parasites can alter their sex ratio in response to the presence of unrelated genotypes within the parasite population.
source: Research on the malaria parasite Plasmodium provides another intriguing example of parasite communication, as studies have revealed that these parasites can alter their sex ratio in response to the presence of unrelated genotypes within the parasite population (Pollitt et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from Pollitt et al., 2011.

claim: EVs isolated from Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigotes lead to parasite spread and survival.
source: In this sense, EVs isolated from Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigotes lead to parasite spread and survival (Trocoli Torrecilhas et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from Trocoli Torrecilhas et al., 2009.

claim: T. brucei EVs promote parasite entrance into host cells.
source: While T. brucei EVs promote parasite entrance into host cells (Atyame Nten et al., 2010; Geiger et al., 2010; Vartak and Gemeinhart, 2007), exosomes also have a role in communication between parasites by affecting social motility and migration (Eliaz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: T. brucei exosomes have a role in communication between parasites by affecting social motility and migration.
source: exosomes also have a role in communication between parasites by affecting social motility and migration (Eliaz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Eliaz et al., 2017.

claim: T. vaginalis EVs possess immunomodulatory properties.
source: In T. vaginalis, EVs have been found to play a crucial role in the pathogenesis of the parasite, as research has shown that they possess immunomodulatory properties and are capable of modulating the adherence of the parasite to host cells. (Nievas et al., 2018a; Olmos-Ortiz et al., 2017; Rai and Johnson, 2019; Twu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: Pre-incubation of small EVs isolated from highly adherent T. vaginalis strains increased the attachment of a poorly adherent strain.
source: In this regard, a previous study showed that pre-incubation of small EVs isolated from highly adherent strains increased the attachment of a poorly adherent strain (Twu et al., 2013), suggesting that small EVs might be involved in both parasite: parasite and parasite: host communication.
evidence: This is cited from Twu et al., 2013.

claim: Previous studies of sEVs and MVs proteomes in B7RC2 strain identified 215 and 592 proteins, respectively.
source: Consistent with this, previous studies of sEVs and MVs proteomes performed in B7RC2 strain identified 215 and 592 proteins, respectively (Nievas et al., 2018b; Twu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Nievas et al., 2018b and Twu et al., 2013.

claim: The sEVs proteome of TV79-49c1 strain contained 1633 proteins.
source: However, when sEVs proteome of TV79-49c1 strain was analyzed, the number of proteins detected in these samples was 1633 (Rada et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from Rada et al., 2022.

claim: EVs released from different T. vaginalis strains may package strain-specific proteins.
source: These and our data (Nievas et al., 2018b; Rada et al., 2022; Twu et al., 2013) suggest that EVs released from different T. vaginalis strains are clearly distinct and may package strain-specific proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of proteomics data across multiple studies.

claim: Proteins from the Rho and Ras family are key regulators in the development of filopodia and cytonemes in other cells.
source: For instance, proteins from the Rho and Ras family, which are part of the RAS superfamily of small GTPases that control cell signaling, have been recognized as key regulators in the development of filopodia and cytonemes in other cells (Koizumi et al., 2012; Kozma et al., 1995; Pellegrin and Mellor, 2005).
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: Calreticulin has been linked to the regulation of cell adhesion and the initiation, stabilization, and turnover of focal contacts.
source: Likewise, a Calreticulin protein identified in the EVs proteomes of all three strains has been linked to the regulation of cell adhesion, as well as the initiation, stabilization, and turnover of focal contacts (Opas et al., 1996; Villagomez et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from Opas et al., 1996 and Villagomez et al., 2009.

claim: Profilin proteins play a critical role in the formation of filopodia.
source: EVs isolated from all three strains contain Profilin proteins, which are small actin-binding proteins known to play a critical role in the formation of filopodia (Rotty et al., 2015; Skruber et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from Rotty et al., 2015 and Skruber et al., 2020.

claim: VPS32 protein is a member of the ESCRT III complex associated with EV biogenesis.
